newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-TOSHACK HOPES TO HALT DEPORTIVO SLIDE AT LEADERS REAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TOSHACK HOPES TO HALT DEPORTIVO SLIDE AT LEADERS REAL.

text.p: Deportivo Coruna manager John Toshack can hardly be relishing the prospect of this weekend's game at Real Madrid, the club he once took to the Spanish championship.

Toshack, who is fighting for his managerial life after a series of bad results, knows that Deportivo have seen their title hopes disappear in three successive years with defeats in the Santiago Bernabeu stadium.

Most Spanish commentators have already written off Deportivo's bid for glory this season. The Galicians have gone five games without a win, and will be left 10 points adrift of leaders Real if they lose again this weekend.
To make matters worse Deportivo have been hit by a series of internal disputes.
Deportivo have opened disciplinary action against the Welshman after he shouted insults to fans in the home match against Athletic Bilbao.
And the wealth of foreign talent at the club is beginning to weigh heavily on the man who each week has to leave full internationals on the bench.
Former Real star Rafael Martin Vazquez and Brazilians Rivaldo and Flavio Conceicao have all complained bitterly to both Toshack and the press after being substituted or dropped.
Toshack's number seemed to be up on Tuesday when his side trailed 2-0 with just 10 minutes on the clock in the Spanish Cup tie with Espanyol.
But Deportivo fought back to equalise, and must have been boosted by the experience.
Real Madrid, on the other hand, lost a 2-1 lead in the 3-2 defeat at arch-rivals Barcelona on Thursday, and with it their unbeaten record under Fabio Capello.
Barcelona manager Bobby Robson could be forgiven for commenting afterwards that Capello's side were 'beatable'.
The former AC Milan coach had been expected to rest some key players ahead of the Deportivo clash, but in the event was forced to employ all his heavy artillery.
The decision may have left him without several key players.
Teenage star Raul Gonzalez is thought to have played the game with a mild fever, and is doubtful for Sunday's match, while central defender Rafael Alkorta was injured in a heavy challenge.
Although the Cup tie is finely-balanced ahead of next week's second leg, the defeat was undoubtedly a bad start to 17 days that could make or break Capello's season.
Real's next home league match will be against Betis, who are riding high at third in the league and are specialists away from home.
Meanwhile victory midweek could have given a vital boost to arch-rivals Barcelona, who stand to close the three-point gap on the leaders in a relatively straightforward home game against Oviedo.
